proposal.summary: Batch N3 covers the round 94 leads: two CM550 prototypes, the CM550 J1708 buffer pointers, the engine position sensor accumulators and the PGN 61442 / TSC1 bytes, plus four CM848 items. scheduleJ1939PeriodicMessage is a proven twin (CM550 0x1fe84 / CM848 0x538c8c). Both bodies have the same steps and store order (+0, +4, +2, +6), the same 20 / 10 queue limits and 19 calls from the datalink start-up. They take (queue, PGN key, interval ms, first send offset ms, builder) and return a byte that no caller reads. cm550_tableLookup2D takes one table_lookup_2d_arguments_t pointer and returns an unsigned word in d0 (it saves every other register). Its CONCAT44 / undefined8 comes only from the missing return type. The J1708 driver uses two 256-byte circular buffers of [length][bytes] records, each with three pointers (message write, byte, message read: e2m JC17TXIP / TXMP / TXOP and RXIP / RXMP / RXOP). io_control_bit0_state is Calterm ESACGR, the accumulated main engine position sensor period between vehicle speed interrupts. The CM848 'fuel demand filter' pair computes and initializes maximum_torque_at_current_engine_speed. The leaf at 0x29ecc is unreachable. The safety_* words belong to the fuel pressure governor fault blend, and every user of governor_tuning_set_blend_weight is an all-speed governor function (Calterm block 158D ASG_Droop_Flag).

functions.role: Appends one periodic J1939 broadcast (PGN key, interval, first send offset, builder) to transmit queue 0 or 1 and returns 1 when that queue is full.
functions.discriminator: It is the only writer of the periodic queues. It fills the entry at count x 10 and increments j1939_periodic_queue0_count / queue1_count (0x800a9a / 0x800a9b; no other code touches them). cm550_runJ1939PeriodicTransmitQueues only reads the entries and advances next_tick. The interval and the offset arrive in ms and are divided by 10 (divs.l #10) into 10 ms ticks.
functions.plate_comment: Adds a periodic J1939 broadcast to transmit queue 0 (the engine node: up to 20 entries of 10 bytes at j1939_periodic_queue0_entries 0x80096e) or queue 1 (the retarder node: up to 10 entries at 0x800a36). The entry gets the PGN key (+0), the interval in 10 ms ticks (+2), the first send as the queue's current tick plus the offset in ticks (+4) and the builder's address (+6). Returns 1 when the queue is full, else 0; no caller reads it. mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink makes all 19 calls through a4 (movea.l #0x1fe84 / jsr (a4)); the first is PGN 65265 every 100 ms from 70 ms. The twin of CM848 0x538c8c: same steps in the same order, the same limits 20 / 10 and the same 19 start-up calls. (PR #53 round 95)
functions.evidence: Entry 0x1fe84: movem.l a3/a2/d2 = 12 bytes, so (0x10;a7) = entry +4, (0x14) = +8, (0x16) = +10, (0x18) = +12, (0x1a) = +14. 0x1fe94 move.l (0x10;a7),d0 / beq queue 0 / cmp.l #1 -> queue 1 (0x1fe9c). 0x1fea2 cmpi.b #0x14,(0x800a9a) / moveq #1,d0 / rts (full). 0x1feb0 index = count++ and entry = 0x80096e + index x 10; d2 = (0x800a9c) the current tick. Queue 1 at 0x1fed4-0x1fefe: limit 0x0a, 0x800a36, tick 0x800a9e. 0x1ff04 move.w (0x14;a7),(a2) = PGN key at +0. 0x1ff08 moveq #0 / move.w (0x18;a7) / divs.l #10 / add.w d2 -> +4. 0x1ff1a same for (0x16;a7) -> +2. 0x1ff2a move.l (0x1a;a7),(0x6;a2) = builder at +6. 0x1ff30 clr.b d0 / rts. CM848 0x538c8c: cmpwi r3,0; lbz count / cmpwi 20 (10) / li r3,1; mulli 10 + 0x3fd2e2 (0x3fd3aa); count+1; lhz tick 0x3fd410 (0x3fd412); sth r4,0 / divw r6,10 + tick -> sth 4 / divw r5,10 -> sth 2 / stw r7,6 / li r3,0. Same store order. Call graph: CM550 has only the raw pointer 0x28b8c (movea.l #0x1fe84,a4 in mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink) and 19 jsr (a4) calls of 14 bytes each. CM848 has 19 bl at 0x5392c0-0x539500, all in cm848_j1939_system_init. The first call in both is PGN 65265, 100 ms, 70 ms, queue 0 (CM550 pea 0x31c84 / 0x46 / 0x64 / 0xfef1 / clr.l; CM848 li r3,0 / ori r4,65265 / li r5,100 / li r6,70).

functions.role: Looks up a z value in a two-axis grid with bilinear interpolation through a 22-byte table_lookup_2d_arguments_t record and returns it as an unsigned word in d0.
functions.discriminator: Its one argument is a record pointer. It searches two axes from the cached segment offsets (+0 and +8), writes the found offsets back and interpolates over the z grid (+16) unless no_interpolation_flag (+20) is nonzero. lookupTableInterpolation 0x34de0 does one axis through table_interp_args_t. The CM848 counterpart cm848_dualAxisTableInterpolation takes seven register arguments and has signed-axis and step options.
functions.plate_comment: Two-axis table lookup through a table_lookup_2d_arguments_t record (the long at +4). It finds the x segment around x_input from x_axis_offset and the y segment around y_input from y_axis_offset (an input outside an axis takes its end point), writes both offsets back as the next search start, and returns the z value as an unsigned word in d0. The value is the grid point interpolated along x, the same for the next y row, then along y (mulu.w / divu.w), or the grid point alone when no_interpolation_flag is nonzero. It saves every register except d0. The 25 callers each push the record and store the word or zero-extend it. CM848's counterpart is cm848_dualAxisTableInterpolation. (PR #53 round 95)
functions.evidence: 0x35088 link a6,#0 / movem.l d1-d6/a0-a5 (every register but d0); 0x35090 movea.l (0x8;a6),a2 = the long at entry +4. x search 0x35094-0x350f6: axis (0x2;a2), input (0x6;a2), offset written back by move.w a1,(a2). y search 0x350f8-0x35160: axis (0xa;a2), input (0xe;a2), offset written back by move.w a5,(0x8;a2). 0x35162-0x35176: grid address = (0x10;a2) + ((y offset - 2) >> 1) x x-axis byte count + x offset - 2. 0x35178 move.w (0x14;a2),d0 / beq; else move.w (a1),d0. Interpolation by mulu.w / divu.w with bcs / bcc (unsigned). Every exit writes only d0.w (0x35180 / 0x351da / 0x35202 / 0x35208 / 0x3521a) and the upper word keeps the divu remainder or the caller's d0, which is where the CONCAT22 / CONCAT44 come from. 25 jsr.l callers (0xad22 ... 0x26ae0): pea record / move.l aN,-(a7); then move.w d0,<dest>, or andi.l #0xffff,d0 at 0x1292a and 0x12c7e.

cm848_functions.role: Computes maximum_torque_at_current_engine_speed (0x40aee6, lb-ft) from the maximum torque map at the filtered engine speed, blended over the combustion chi maps and alpha.
cm848_functions.discriminator: It is the periodic writer of maximum_torque_at_current_engine_speed (the init is the only other one). It makes three cm848_dualAxisTableInterpolation lookups of maximum_torque_map_grid, at y = 0 and at y = combustion_chi_lower / upper_map_number << 14 (capped 0xffff), each with its own cache (0x3faf98 / 0x3faf9c / 0x3fafa0). It blends them with cm848_interpolateAlphaChiValue and replaces 0 by 1. Nothing in it filters fuel demand. CM550's counterpart makes one lookup (engine speed x alpha).
cm848_functions.plate_comment: Computes the maximum engine torque at the current engine speed (CHR e2m 1461 +0 MT_Max_Torque_At_RPM_Ftlb, lb-ft) into maximum_torque_at_current_engine_speed. It looks up maximum_torque_map_grid (e2m MT_Max_Torque_Map over MT_RPM_Axis and MT_Alpha_Axis) at engine_speed_state.filtered_engine_speed in the alpha 0 row and in the rows of combustion_chi_lower_map_number and combustion_chi_upper_map_number (x 0x4000). It blends them by combustion_reference_state.chi_hundredths and alpha_percent with cm848_interpolateAlphaChiValue and replaces 0 by 1 (the value is a divisor). Called by cm848_periodicTaskSet_sensorProcessing. CM550's counterpart cm550_calculateMaximumTorqueAtCurrentEngineSpeed makes one lookup over engine speed and alpha. (was cm848_calculateFuelDemandFilter; PR #53 round 95)
cm848_functions.evidence: 0x29ca8-0x29cbc: r26 = 0x5c58e grid, r27 = 0x5c582 y axis, r28 = 0x5c556 x axis, r30 = 0x40b7ba engine speed. bl 0x566cc at 0x29ce8 (cache 0x3faf98, y 0), 0x29d30 (0x3faf9c, chi lower << 14) and 0x29d78 (0x3fafa0, chi upper << 14). bl 0x14528 cm848_interpolateAlphaChiValue at 0x29dac. 0x29d80 r31 = 0x410000 - 20762 = 0x40aee6; 0x29db4 sth r29,0(r31); 0x29dbc cmpwi 0 / li 1 / sth at 0x29dc8. The only stores are those two. Caller: cm848_periodicTaskSet_sensorProcessing (0xb98c). CM550 0x269f2: one cm550_tableLookup2D with engine_rpm_primary and alpha_blend_factor, then min 1. RAM dump 0x40aee6 = 0x0122 (290 lb-ft).

cm848_functions.role: Start-up: sets maximum_torque_at_current_engine_speed to 1 and the three maximum torque map lookup caches to 2.
cm848_functions.discriminator: It writes only 0x40aee6 (1) and the six cache words 0x3faf98-0x3fafa2 (2), and is called once from cm848_applicationMain. The other start-up initializers set other records, for example cm848_initializeInjectionTimingMainMisfireLimit at 0x29e24.
cm848_functions.plate_comment: Start-up initialization of cm848_calculateMaximumTorqueAtCurrentEngineSpeed. It sets maximum_torque_at_current_engine_speed to 1 and both words of maximum_torque_map_alpha_0_cached_axis_offsets, maximum_torque_map_chi_lower_cached_axis_offsets and maximum_torque_map_chi_upper_cached_axis_offsets to 2 (the first axis point). Called once from cm848_applicationMain. CM550's counterpart is cm550_initializeMaximumTorqueAtCurrentEngineSpeed. (was cm848_initFuelDemandFilterDimensions; PR #53 round 95)
cm848_functions.evidence: 0x29de0 lis r12,0x41 / li r11,1 / sth r11,-20762(r12) = 0x40aee6. li r3,2 / sth to 0(r4) and 2(r4) for r4 = 0x3faf98, 0x3faf9c and 0x3fafa0 (0x29df0-0x29e1c). blr 0x29e20. Caller: cm848_applicationMain 0x544c4 (decompile line 59130). CM550 0x26a2e sets the torque to 1 and points maximum_torque_map_lookup at its tables with offsets 2.

cm848_functions.role: Unreachable leaf. While the misfire timing limit is enabled and the intermediate timing source is the 4D maps, it saves main_injection_timing_copy as main_injection_timing_before_misfire_limit and raises the copy to injection_timing_main_misfire_limit (source code 11).
cm848_functions.discriminator: It works on main_injection_timing_copy, injection_timing_intermediate_source_code and bit 0 of injection_timing_increment_flags. It is the only store of main_injection_timing_before_misfire_limit besides the power-up clear. The live misfire limit is applied to injection_timing_demand inside cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming (0x4ae20), which sets main_injection_timing_source_code. No branch, address word, lis+addi or lis+ori pair in the ROM or the flash2 image reaches 0x29ecc, so it is dead under any calibration.
cm848_functions.plate_comment: Dead code: nothing calls it (no branch, address word or lis+addi / lis+ori pair in the ROM or the flash2 image reaches 0x29ecc). While algorithm_enable_flags_40_cal bit 8 (e2m Misfire_Timing_Limit_Enable) is set and injection_timing_intermediate_source_code is 0 (the 4D maps), it copies main_injection_timing_copy into main_injection_timing_before_misfire_limit (e2m 8A3D +2 SOI_Before_MST). When injection_timing_main_misfire_limit is larger (signed) it raises main_injection_timing_copy to it, clears bit 0 of injection_timing_increment_flags and sets the intermediate source code to 11 (e2m 103B label 0B MISFIRE). The live misfire limit is the injection_timing_demand step of cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming. (new row; PR #53 round 95)
cm848_functions.evidence: ROM 0x29ecc-0x29f38: the previous blr is at 0x29ec8 (cm848_calculateInjectionTimingMainMisfireLimit) and cm848_absoluteValue16 starts at 0x29f3c. lhz 0x3fd5ec / rlwinm 0,23,23 (0x100) / beq out. lha 0x40a2f2 / bne out. lha 0x40a2f0 -> sth 0x40aeea (0x29f04). lha 0x40aee8 / cmpw / ble out. sth to 0x40a2f0 (0x29f18); lhz 0x40a2f4 / rlwinm 16,30 / sth; li r10,11 / sth 0x40a2f2; blr. ppc_refs.py over both images found nothing for 0x29ecc; the same scan finds bl 0x29e50 at 0xbab0. The frozen .cpp has no function at 0x29ecc. RAM dump 0x40aeea = 0. Live path: cm848_calculateMainInjectionTiming 'if (injection_timing_demand < injection_timing_main_misfire_limit)' -> MAIN_INJECTION_TIMING_SOURCE_MISFIRE_LIMIT.

params.name: queue_index
params.comment: The queue - the long at +4 (move.l (0x10;a7) after the 12-byte movem): 0 = queue 0 j1939_periodic_queue0_entries (the engine node) / 1 = queue 1 j1939_periodic_queue1_entries (the retarder node); the callers push clr.l or pea (1).w (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: pgn_key
params.comment: The PGN key stored at the entry's +0 - the word at +8 (move.w (0x14;a7);(a2)): 65265 / 61444 / 61443 / ... (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: interval_milliseconds
params.comment: The transmit interval in ms - the word at +10 (moveq #0 / move.w (0x16;a7) / divs.l #10) - kept in the entry's +2 as 10 ms ticks (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: first_send_offset_milliseconds
params.comment: The delay of the first send in ms - the word at +12 (move.w (0x18;a7) / divs.l #10) - added to the queue's current tick into the entry's +4 (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: builder
params.comment: The message builder - the long at +14 (move.l (0x1a;a7);(0x6;a2)) - that cm550_runJ1939PeriodicTransmitQueues calls when its tick comes (PR #53 round 95)

prototypes.evidence: Stack layout: first_stack_offset 4 and slot 2 give +4 (4 bytes) / +8 / +10 / +12 (2 bytes each) / +14 (4 bytes). The body reads exactly those offsets after its 12-byte movem.l a3/a2/d2: (0x10) move.l, (0x14) move.w, (0x16) move.w zero-extended, (0x18) move.w zero-extended, (0x1a) move.l. The callers push pea builder / move.w offset / move.w interval / move.w PGN / clr.l (or pea (1).w) queue = 14 bytes per call (lea (0x2a;a7) after every 3). Return: moveq #1,d0 (full) or clr.b d0 (only the low byte defined) -> byte; no caller reads d0 (the next push follows each jsr (a4)). The function's body is missing from the frozen and the current .cpp (see notes), but the callers render its name, so the function record exists.

params.name: queue_index
params.comment: The queue (r3; cmpwi r3,0): 0 = queue 0 at 0x3fd2e2 (the engine node; 20 entries) / any other value = queue 1 at 0x3fd3aa (the retarder node; 10 entries) (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: pgn_key
params.comment: The PGN key (r4) stored with sth at the entry's +0 (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: interval_milliseconds
params.comment: The transmit interval in ms (r5): divw by 10 into the entry's +2 (a full 32-bit divide; a 16-bit type would leave CONCAT22 artifacts) (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: first_send_offset_milliseconds
params.comment: The delay of the first send in ms (r6): divw by 10 plus the queue's current tick into the entry's +4 (PR #53 round 95)

params.name: builder
params.comment: The message builder (r7) stored with stw at the entry's +6; the periodic transmit code calls it when its tick comes (PR #53 round 95)

prototypes.evidence: 0x538c8c cmpwi r3,0; 0x538d10 sth r4,0(r3); 0x538d18 divw r12,r6,10 + tick -> sth 4; 0x538d28 divw r11,r5,10 -> sth 2; 0x538d30 stw r7,6(r3); li r3,1 at 0x538ca8 / 0x538ce8 (full) and li r3,0 at 0x538d34. Callers (19 bl in cm848_j1939_system_init) load r3 queue, r4 PGN (lis 0 / ori), r5 interval, r6 offset and r7 builder (lis / addi). The instruction after each bl is lis r7 for the next call, so no caller reads r3. Same parameter names as CM848 registerJ1939ReceiveHandler (pgn_key ushort, handler void*).

params.name: lookup
params.comment: The 22-byte argument record - the long at +4 (movea.l (0x8;a6);a2 after link a6): axes / inputs / grid / no-interpolation flag; the function writes back the found x_axis_offset (+0) and y_axis_offset (+8) (was table_args short*; PR #53 round 95)

prototypes.evidence: 0x35088 link a6,#0 then movea.l (0x8;a6),a2 = the long at entry +4: one 4-byte parameter, and each of the 25 callers pushes one long (pea record / move.l aN,-(a7)). The movem.l saves d1-d6/a0-a5, so d0 is the only result. Every exit writes d0 with a word operation only (move.w (a1),d0 / add.w / sub.w / the divu.w quotient). The upper word is the divu.w remainder or the caller's old d0, which is why the undeclared return renders as CONCAT22 / CONCAT44 (undefined8). Unsigned throughout (bcs / bcc, mulu.w / divu.w). Callers: move.w d0,<global or (aN)> or move.w d0,dN, and andi.l #0xffff,d0 at 0x1292a and 0x12c7e (zero-extend), so the return is an unsigned word. Return row: 0x00035088,cm550_tableLookup2D,return,,word,...

globals.comment: e2m 1126 +0 JC17TXIP: where the next queued J1708 message goes in the 256-byte transmit buffer at 0x808b00 (records of [length][bytes]); it always points at a 0 length (the end marker). The message writers compute the free space as j1708_transmit_buffer_read_pointer minus it (minus 2, plus 0xfe when it wraps), write the record there and move it past the record. The pointers step only their low byte, so they wrap inside the 256 bytes. RAM dump 0x808b7d = the read pointer (queue empty). (was j1708_transmit_buffer_0_2_32; PR #53 round 95)
globals.evidence: Init 0x1dd48 = 0x808bdc & 0xffffff00 = 0x808b00; 0x1dd60 clr.b (it). Writer cm550_diagnosticMessageQueueWrite 0xb708-0xb72c: (0x80dc9c) - (0x80dc94) free check; 0xb732 record start = it; 0xb786 move.l (a2),(0x80dc94); 0xb78e clr.b. Same pattern in the many builders (0x1e810 / 0x1f2ea / 0x1fc10 ...). ISRs compare it with the read pointer to find pending messages (0x1e316 / 0x1e4f8 / 0x30200).

globals.comment: e2m 1126 +4 JC17TXMP: the byte of the current J1708 message that is being sent. mc68k_startJ1708Transmission writes *pointer to the SCI data register. mc68k_j1708SciInterruptHandler compares the echo of the first byte with it (bus arbitration), then steps its low byte and sends the next byte until the record's length is reached, then sends the checksum. After the checksum it points at the next record's length byte, which becomes the read pointer. The bus timer handler rewinds it to the read pointer + 1 to resend. RAM dump 0x808b7e. (was j1708_transmit_buffer_2_32_dc98; PR #53 round 95)
globals.evidence: Init 0x1dd4e (0x4;a1) = TXIP then addq.b #1,(0x7;a1). mc68k_startJ1708Transmission 0x16d7c movea.l #0x80dc98,a2 / move.b (a0) -> 0xfffc0e. ISR 0x1e35e-0x1e368 a2 = a4 + 4, cmp.b (a0),d2 (echo). 0x1e3ca / 0x1e414 addq.b #1,(0x7;a4) then send *(0x4;a4). 0x1e470 addq.b after the checksum. 0x1e480 move.l (0x4;a4),(0x8;a4). Bus timer ISR 0x301d4 move.l (0x8;a3),(0x4;a3) / addq.b #1,(0x7;a3) and 0x3021a sends *(a3 + 4).

globals.comment: e2m 1126 +8 JC17TXOP: the length byte of the J1708 message being sent (the oldest unsent message). The SCI interrupt handler ends the data bytes when its byte count equals *pointer, and moves the pointer to the next record after the checksum. The writers' free space is it minus the write pointer. A message is pending while the write pointer differs from it. (was j1708_transmit_buffer_2_32_dc9c; PR #53 round 95)
globals.evidence: Init 0x1dd46 move.l d0,(a2) with a2 = 0x80dc9c. ISR 0x1e3f4 / 0x1e442 movea.l (0x8;a4),a0 / cmp.b (a0),d0 (count vs length). 0x1e480 move.l (0x4;a4),(0x8;a4). Writers 0xb6f8 movea.l #0x80dc9c,a3 / move.l (a3),d0 / sub.l TXIP (0x16724 / 0x1ee9a / 0x1f2f4 same). ISRs 0x1e31c / 0x1e4fe / 0x30206 cmp.l (0x8;a4) with TXIP.

globals.comment: e2m 1126 +0x0E JC17RXIP: the length byte of the J1708 message being received in the 256-byte receive buffer at 0x808c00. The SCI interrupt handler adds 1 to *pointer for each byte it stores. mc68k_j1708BusTimerInterruptHandler closes the message on bus idle. With a good checksum it removes the checksum byte from the count and moves the pointer to that byte's slot, the next record. A message under 3 bytes or with a bad checksum is discarded instead. mc68k_dispatchJ1708ReceivedMessages handles records until its read pointer reaches this one. RAM dump 0x808c00. (was j1708_receive_buffer_pointer_2_32_dca2; PR #53 round 95)
globals.evidence: Init 0x1dd74-0x1dd90 a2 = a1 + 14: move.l d0,(a2) (0x808c00) / clr.b (a0). ISR 0x1e2ce / 0x1e38c movea.l (0xe;a4),a0 / addq.b #1,(a0). 0x1e2e8-0x1e2f2 compares it with the read pointer when the buffer is full. Bus timer ISR 0x300de a4 = a3 + 14: tst.b (a0) / cmpi.b #3 / 0x301b0 subq.b #1,(a0) / 0x301b2-0x301ba low byte = byte pointer - 1 / 0x301c0 clr.b. Reader 0x16440 move.l (0x80dca2),d0 / cmp.l (a3) (read pointer) / bne loop.

globals.comment: e2m 1126 +0x12 JC17RXMP: where mc68k_j1708SciInterruptHandler stores the next received J1708 byte (then it steps the low byte). The receive buffer is full when it reaches the read pointer. The bus timer handler resets it to the write pointer + 1 when it discards a message. RAM dump 0x808c01. (was j1708_receive_buffer_pointer_2_32_dca6; PR #53 round 95)
globals.evidence: Init 0x1dd86 (0x12;a1) = RXIP / addq.b #1,(0x15;a1). ISR 0x1e2c4 movea.l (0x12;a4),a0 / move.b d2,(a0) / addq.b #1,(0x15;a4); 0x1e382-0x1e388 the same on the first byte after a lost arbitration; 0x1e2e0 / 0x1e396 cmp.l with (0x16;a4) for full. Bus timer ISR 0x30128-0x3012e / 0x30140-0x30146 / 0x3019c-0x301a2 move.b to (0x15;a3) = write pointer low byte + 1; 0x3014a movea.l (0x12;a3) / cmpi.b #7,(a0).

globals.comment: e2m 1126 +0x16 JC17RXOP: the length byte of the oldest unprocessed J1708 message. mc68k_dispatchJ1708ReceivedMessages handles the record there, adds its length + 1 to the pointer's low byte, clears the receive buffer full flag and re-enables the SCI receive interrupt. The receive side stops (full) when the byte pointer reaches it. (was j1708_receive_buffer_pointer_2_32_dcaa; PR #53 round 95)
globals.evidence: Init 0x1dd82 move.l d0,(a3) with a3 = a1 + 22. Reader 0x15fbe movea.l #0x80dcaa,a3 / 0x15fce move.l (a3),(-4;a6) / move.b (a0),d3 (length); 0x16416-0x1641a add.b d0,(0x80dcad) (length + 1); 0x16420 clr.b full flag; 0x16422 ori.w #0x20 SCCR1. Multi-packet handlers 0x16680 / 0x16884 and the diagnostic handlers read it (move.l (abs) at 0x1e966 / 0x1ec48 / 0x1edc6 / 0x1eece / 0x1f504 / 0x1f866 / 0x1f8d8 / 0x1fbba).

globals.comment: e2m 1127 +0 JC17TXBF 'J1708 TRANSMIT BUFFER': holds the address of the 256-byte J1708 transmit buffer (0x808b00), written once by cm550_diagnosticBufferPointerInit; no code reads it (only the parameter ID table lists it, for Calterm). roles.role: Adds one periodic J1939 broadcast to transmit queue 0 (20 x 10-byte entries at 0x80096e, count 0x800a9a, tick 0x800a9c) or queue 1 (10 entries at 0x800a36, count 0x800a9b, tick 0x800a9e). Entry fields: +0 the PGN, +2 the interval ms / 10, +4 the queue's current tick + first-send offset ms / 10, +6 the builder. Returns 1 (moveq) when the queue is full, else clears d0.b. PROTOTYPE: byte scheduleJ1939PeriodicMessage(dword queue_index @+4, ushort pgn @+8, ushort interval_milliseconds @+10, ushort first_send_offset_milliseconds @+12, void* builder @+14).
roles.discriminator: The only function that writes a j1939_periodic_transmit_entry_t; cm550_runJ1939PeriodicTransmitQueues reads the entries. After a 12-byte movem the body reads move.l (0x10,a7) / move.w (0x14,a7) / move.w (0x16,a7) / move.w (0x18,a7) / move.l (0x1a,a7) = entry offsets +4 / +8 / +10 / +12 / +14, which fits stack_parameter_layout. moveq #0 / move.w then divs.l #10: the words are zero-extended. Success ends with clr.b d0 only, so the return is a byte. Only caller: mc68k_initializeJ1939Datalink (movea.l #0x1fe84,a4 at 0x28b8a, then 19 x jsr (a4)). Each call pushes pea builder, move.w offset, move.w interval, move.w PGN (0xfef1 = 65265 ...), then clr.l or pea (1).w; the caller pops 3 calls at a time with lea 0x2a = 3 x 14 bytes and never reads d0. A queue other than 0 / 1 skips the setup and writes through the caller's a2. The frozen .cpp has no body at 0x1fe84 and shows the calls as scheduleJ1939PeriodicMessage(0,100).
